children: Anup Bagchi takes charge as HDFC Bank’s first external CEO, with growth, margins, deposits and governance now firmly on the agenda
For HDFC Bank, the succession question has finally been answered. The harder question begins on 27 October.

Anup Bagchi, currently Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, will take over as HDFC Bank’s MD & CEO for a three-year term, succeeding Sashidhar Jagdishan. His appointment, approved by the Reserve Bank of India, also makes him the first external candidate to occupy the bank’s top executive position.

The timing makes the appointment more consequential than a routine CEO transition. HDFC Bank is operating with a substantially larger balance sheet following its merger with HDFC Ltd, while investors have been watching deposit mobilisation, loan growth, margins and return ratios closely. In FY2025-26, the bank’s deposits grew 14.4 per cent and advances 12.1 per cent, while profit after tax increased 10.9 per cent. Its return on equity stood at 14.3 per cent and net interest margin at 3.34 per cent for the year.

The numbers do not point to a bank in distress. They do, however, explain why the market is looking closely at what comes next. HDFC Bank itself has acknowledged that the HDFC Ltd transaction affected margins because the mortgage lender brought a relatively lower-yielding asset mix and higher cost of funds. As of 31 March 2026, current and savings account deposits accounted for 34.1 per cent of total deposits.

That makes Bagchi’s mandate less about a dramatic turnaround and more about execution. Analysts have identified deposit mobilisation, sustaining loan growth, margin recovery and return ratios as key areas to watch, while also pointing to the importance of clarity around the bank’s medium-term strategy.

Bagchi brings a distinctly broad financial-services background to that task. He has been associated with the ICICI Group since 1992 and has worked across treasury, retail banking, wholesale banking, investment banking and digital financial services. He served as Executive Director at ICICI Bank from 2017 to 2023, overseeing retail, business and rural banking before moving to wholesale banking, and subsequently led ICICI Securities and ICICI Prudential Life Insurance.

His outsider status is therefore significant, but not because he arrives without banking experience. Rather, he brings experience from another large private-sector financial-services franchise at a point when HDFC Bank is entering its next phase of growth. Analysts have specifically flagged the need to manage the transition between the two institutional cultures while maintaining continuity in the senior management team.

There is also a governance backdrop to the transition. Former part-time chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned in March, saying certain “happenings and practices” at the bank were not consistent with his personal values and ethics. HDFC Bank subsequently commissioned an independent legal review, which concluded that the allegations were not substantiated by the documentary evidence and witness interviews examined. Chakraborty did not participate in that review.

The governance episode is therefore part of the context, rather than evidence by itself of a continuing governance problem. What matters for the new leadership is how the bank communicates its strategy, manages stakeholders and maintains confidence while executing on a much larger post-merger franchise.

The leadership transition is also taking place alongside changes to HDFC Bank’s senior management structure. The bank has proposed Jimmy Tata, its Chief Credit Officer, as an additional whole-time director and has sought the reappointment of V Srinivasa Rangan as a whole-time director. The changes indicate that the CEO appointment is occurring within a broader exercise in strengthening the leadership architecture of the bank.

For Bagchi, then, the first few months are unlikely to be about proving that HDFC Bank needs a new identity. The more immediate task will be to establish where the existing model needs adjustment, where the post-merger balance sheet can generate greater efficiency and how the bank can make its next phase of growth more predictable.
The succession uncertainty may now be over. The execution test has just begun.
